points.description: States that the algorithm must be implemented (written as actual code or a program) so it can be run. Equivalent wording such as 'write a program for the algorithm' earns the mark.

States that the running time is measured physically, i.e. by running the implementation and recording the elapsed (wall-clock or CPU) time. Equivalent wording such as 'time the program on test inputs with a clock' earns the mark. Describing the measurement as an analysis of operation counts or a theoretical estimate does not earn this mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for an answer that says the algorithm is implemented and that its physical running time is measured by running it. Award 2 for implementation alone and 3 for measuring elapsed time by running the code; an answer giving only the theoretical or operation-counting approach earns no marks. Do not require the exact model wording.
